Consult Summary:
- Acute unilateral left-ear hearing loss with left facial numbness, accompanied by intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness for ~3 weeks; patient referred for in-person neurological and ENT assessment to confirm a potential Bell’s palsy and exclude other causes; appointment to be scheduled in Central London.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left-sided hearing loss with numbness of the left face (jawline area) for several weeks; associated intermittent tinnitus; no weakness elsewhere, no dysphagia, no dysarthria, no vision changes.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~3 weeks ago; numbness is ongoing and present at the time of evaluation; hearing loss described as decreased hearing on the left.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not documented.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent tinnitus; occasional dizziness when tinnitus occurs.
- ROS/negative findings: No fever; no ear discharge; no ear pain; no discharge; no facial weakness reported beyond numbness; no systemic symptoms.
- Relevant negatives: No difficulty swallowing or speaking; no vision problems; no other neurological symptoms reported.
- Self-care/initiating measures: Not documented.
- Additional context: Worried about seriousness; asked for reassurance; patient currently working as a jockey and reports some training impairment due to symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps (past history; intermittently treated with nasal spray).
- Prior labyrinthitis (history mentioned; not described as active).
- Medications: Nasal spray (PRN; exact name not documented); Rennies PRN.
- Allergies: Latex.
- Others: No other chronic illnesses noted.

Social History:
- Occupation: Jockey; currently training reduced due to symptoms.
- Living situation: Lives with partner.
- Pets: None.
- Tobacco/alcohol/drug use: Not documented.

Family History:
- Brother with Neurofibromatosis.
- No other family medical history stated.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Unilateral left-sided hearing loss with left facial numbness (possible Bell’s palsy; differential includes other unilateral facial/ear pathologies).
  - Plan:
    - Require in-person neurological examination and ENT/ear examination today to confirm diagnosis.
    - Arrangements: Admin to book a face-to-face clinic visit in Central London; patient advised to contact support line to obtain an appointment as soon as possible.
    - Education/reassurance: Not life-threatening based on current information; planned physical examination needed for definitive reassurance.
- Issue 2: Intermittent tinnitus and occasional dizziness.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate during in-person assessment; no specific acute treatment prescribed at this time.
- Issue 3: Medical history and safety considerations.
  - Plan:
    - Document latex allergy.
    - Continue PRN nasal spray for polyps if needed; Rennies PRN as before; no new medications prescribed at this time.
    - No acute home management changes discussed.

General plan:
- Attend scheduled in-person clinic today for full neurological exam and otoscopic ear exam to assess for Bell’s palsy or alternative etiologies.
- Reassure patient with preliminary assessment; definitive reassurance contingent on physical examination.
- Follow-up to be determined based on exam findings and any additional testing.
